description: Golden cases for the news digest eval (NEWS-SUMMARY-EVAL-PLAN.md, layer 3). Each case pins a headline set to a frozen `asOf` time so recency labels do not drift as the fixtures age. `expectedOutcome` is what the pipeline should do; `acceptableCloserKeys` is a set, not one right answer, because more than one standing fact can legitimately match. Historical cases carry the text that actually published and the failure it must be caught by.
status: PROPOSED — labels drafted by Claude 2026-09-12, awaiting Andria's approval. Not yet a pass/fail gate.

cases.note: Published. The invented date is the one error the deterministic gates catch.

headlines.title: More Than a Year Later, National Guard Troops Still Patrol D.C. as ACLU Demands Their Exit
Eyeing the midterm elections, D.C. is taking the fight for statehood to the states
VIDEO: Senator Slotkin Commits to Making DC Statehood a Top Priority

cases.publishedBody: More than a year after events in January 2021, National Guard troops continue to patrol D.C. as civil rights advocates call for their withdrawal, while statehood supporters are intensifying advocacy efforts ahead of midterm elections, including gaining commitments from elected officials.

cases.note: Published. Passes every deterministic gate; only the judge sees it.

headlines.title: Eyeing the midterm elections, D.C. is taking the fight for statehood to the states
What D.C. residents will remember from a year of National Guard occupation
One Year After President Trump Deployed National Guard Troops to Washington, D.C., Statehood is More Important Than Ever

cases.publishedBody: D.C. statehood advocates are marking the anniversary of National Guard deployment to the District while intensifying advocacy efforts ahead of the midterm elections. The deployment, which lasted a year, is being highlighted by advocacy groups as evidence for why D.C. needs greater autonomy.
cases.failureMode: F2 unsupported inference — an anniversary is not an ending

cases.note: Published. RELABELLED 2026-09-12 on Andria's call: 39 days is inside the ~2-month window this beat moves on, so 'currently considering' is acceptable language, not an error. Kept as a case because the same body calls a takeover from 12+ months earlier 'recent', which is outside the window — borderline, so it scores neither as a required catch nor as a precision control.

headlines.title: Eyeing the midterm elections, D.C. is taking the fight for statehood to the states
One Year Later, DC Vote Says Federal Takeover Underscores the Urgency of DC Statehood
DC Vote Urges House Committee to Reject Sweeping Attack on DC's Fiscal Independence

cases.publishedBody: Recent federal interventions in D.C.—including a takeover and National Guard deployment—have prompted advocates to emphasize how statehood would protect the District, and a House committee is currently considering proposals that advocates say would further undermine D.C.'s fiscal independence.

cases.note: The failure Andria named: saying something is under consideration when the headline says it already happened. This is the J3 case that matters, replacing the tense-nuance ones.

headlines.title: House votes 214-209 to overturn D.C. policing law
Senate sends D.C. budget rider to the President's desk

cases.publishedBody: The House is currently considering whether to overturn a District policing law, while senators continue to debate a rider affecting D.C.'s budget.
cases.failureMode: F5 decided matters described as still pending

cases.note: Produced by the REWRITTEN pipeline in its first dry run. RELABELLED TWICE on 2026-09-12. First as acceptable (53 days is inside the ~2-month window), then back to an error once the judge explained itself: the headline has DC Vote urging Congress to REJECT a proposed attack on fiscal independence, so 'ongoing restrictions on how DC can use its budget' presents a pending proposal as something already in force. That is the mirror of the decided-called-pending failure and the same class Andria cares about — the age of the headline was never the issue.

cases.note: Judge-precision control. The false-alarm rate is measured against THIS labelled body — attributed, correctly dated, no legal claim — not against a fresh generation. The judge must not flag it.

cases.note: Seeded J2 case: the body states a power, which is the closer's job and was wrong twice when the model wrote it freely.
